definition: People can see that AI is in use, what it is for, and where an output came from (data, sources, logic).
includes: Disclosing AI use; labelling AI-generated content; documentation such as model cards; tracing an answer back to its sources.
excludes: Explaining why a particular output was produced (EXP). Records kept so someone can be held to account (ACC).
borderline_decision: VURA "Visible" (trace where an answer came from): TRA, because it is about seeing the source, not about why.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Jobin: transparency. Fjeld: transparency and explainability.
why_separate: The most common principle in 2019. Kept apart from explainability because the two come apart for LLMs: you can show sources without being able to explain the model's reasoning.

definition: Users or reviewers can understand why the system produced a particular output, in terms they can follow.
includes: Explanations of outputs; interpretable logic; outputs that business experts can check against their own understanding.
excludes: Disclosing that AI is used (TRA). General AI literacy for staff (LIT).
borderline_decision: VURA "Understandable": EXP. UK principle "You know what AI is and what its limitations are": LIT (from v1.1), because it is about staff skills, not about explaining outputs.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Jobin: inside transparency. Fjeld: joined with transparency.
why_separate: Split from transparency so we can test prediction 4: that explainability is among the hardest dimensions for practitioners.

definition: Named people or bodies answer for the system and its outcomes, with the records and routes needed to check and challenge them.
includes: Owners and roles; governance bodies; audit trails; audits; redress and the right to contest outcomes.
excludes: Disclosing that AI is used (TRA). People stepping in while the system runs (HUM).
borderline_decision: VURA "Auditable": ACC, not HUM. A record of oversight is not oversight (adjudication decision 6).
in_2019_2020_reviews: Jobin: responsibility. Fjeld: accountability; professional responsibility.
why_separate: Audit trails go here, not under transparency, because their purpose is that someone can be held to account.

definition: Outputs and decisions do not treat people or groups unfairly; bias is found and reduced.
includes: Bias testing; non-discrimination; equal treatment of groups.
borderline_decision: Microsoft "Inclusiveness" (AI should empower everyone): SOC, unless its description is about bias or discrimination.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Jobin: justice and fairness. Fjeld: fairness and non-discrimination.
why_separate: Prediction 2 expects fairness to lose ground for generative AI, so code it only where the item is about fairness, not every mention of people.

definition: Personal data is collected, used and kept lawfully and sparingly, and people keep control over it.
includes: Data protection; consent; data minimisation; keeping personal data out of prompts and outputs.
excludes: Protection against attackers (SEC). Quality and provenance of data (DAT).
borderline_decision: A combined label such as AWS "Privacy and security": code both PRI and SEC as named; primary is whichever the description stresses.
why_separate: Combined labels are common. The rule is to split them rather than pick one.

definition: The system and its data are protected against deliberate attack and misuse, from outside or inside.
includes: Prompt injection; data poisoning; model theft; access control; red teaming aimed at attacks.
excludes: Harmful outputs where no attacker is involved (SAF).
borderline_decision: Red teaming for harmful content rather than attacks: SAF.
why_separate: Split from safety because prediction 3 expects security to rise with agents, which read untrusted content and take actions.

definition: The system does not cause harm through its outputs or its use: harmful content, dangerous advice, misuse.
includes: Content filtering; testing for harmful content; preventing misuse; catastrophic risks such as chemical or biological weapons information.
borderline_decision: NIST risk "dangerous, violent or hateful content": SAF. A wrong answer is REL unless the description stresses harm.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Jobin: non-maleficence. Fjeld: safety and security.
why_separate: Safety is about harm; reliability is about being right.

definition: Outputs are correct and the system performs as intended, including on unexpected inputs.
includes: Accuracy; hallucination (NIST calls it confabulation); robustness; validity.
excludes: Getting the same answer for the same input (RPR). The process of testing (TST).
borderline_decision: NIST risk "confabulation": REL, because a risk is coded to the dimension that addresses it.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Not a separate theme in either review.
why_separate: Expected to be new and prominent for generative AI (prediction 3).

definition: The same inputs, data and instructions give the same output, and the setup that produced it can be rerun.
includes: Repeatability; version control of prompts, models and workflows; documented processes that others can rerun.
excludes: Whether a single output is correct (REL).
borderline_decision: VURA "Repeatable": RPR. An item that says the system should perform "reliably and consistently" without naming repeatability: REL primary, RPR mentioned.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Not in either review. AI Verify names repeatability and reproducibility.
why_separate: Kept separate in v0 (open decision). Merging later is easy; splitting later means recoding everything. It also tests how rarely frameworks name repeatability, which matters for deterministic pathways such as fixed scripts and pre-approved queries.

definition: People can monitor, approve, override or stop the system, and are equipped to do so.
includes: Human in the loop; approval before actions; escalation; the ability to switch the system off.
excludes: Limits built into what an agent can do (ACT). Named ownership (ACC).
borderline_decision: Australia "Maintain human control": HUM. Guidance on human approval checkpoints for agents: HUM. Guidance on limiting an agent's tool access: ACT.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Fjeld: human control of technology. Jobin: partly freedom and autonomy.
why_separate: Oversight is about people stepping in.

definition: What the system may do is bounded by design: permissions, tool and system access, spending or data limits, how far it acts on its own.
includes: Least privilege; restricted tool access; sandboxing; limits on autonomy.
borderline_decision: Limit the agent's access to tools and external systems: ACT.
why_separate: New for agents (prediction 3). Separate from human oversight because a limit works even when nobody is watching.

definition: Risks and impacts are identified and assessed before and during use, in proportion to the stakes.
includes: Risk assessment; impact assessment; risk tiers; screening use cases.
borderline_decision: Australia "Understand impacts and plan accordingly": RSK. NIST's four functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) are its structure, not items: code NIST's listed characteristics and risks instead.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Not a principle in either review.
why_separate: A practice, not a value. Included because government frameworks are built around it; it lets us test whether governments publish practices and companies publish principles.

definition: The system is evaluated before release and watched after it, with results recorded.
includes: Evaluation before deployment; red teaming as a process; ongoing monitoring; incident reporting.
excludes: The property being tested: code that as well (REL, SAF, FAI and so on), as mentioned.
borderline_decision: Australia "Test and monitor": TST primary; add the property tested as mentioned only if the description names it.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Not a principle in either review.
why_separate: Like RSK, a practice. Separating the process from the property shows which frameworks say how to check, not just what to aim for.

definition: Data used by or fed to the system is fit for purpose: quality, provenance, lineage, rights to use it.
includes: Data quality; provenance; data integrity; documentation of training data.
excludes: Personal data protection (PRI). Copyright as a legal duty (LAW).
in_2019_2020_reviews: Not a theme in either review. AI Verify names data governance.
why_separate: Poor or fragmented data is a common barrier in surveys of AI adoption; this dimension shows which frameworks address it.

definition: The system complies with applicable law, including intellectual property and copyright.
includes: Lawful use; copyright policy; regulatory compliance.
borderline_decision: EU GPAI Code "Copyright" chapter: LAW. UK principle "You use AI lawfully, ethically and responsibly": LAW primary, ACC mentioned.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Not a theme in either review.
why_separate: Generative AI raised copyright questions that rule-based systems did not.

definition: AI benefits people and society and limits its environmental cost.
includes: Sustainability and energy use; inclusion and accessibility; human wellbeing.
in_2019_2020_reviews: Jobin: beneficence, sustainability, dignity, solidarity. Fjeld: promotion of human values.
why_separate: Groups several 2019 values that rarely carry practical steps for a project team.

definition: Fits none of the dimensions above.
includes: Always add a note naming the theme.
borderline_decision: If three or more frameworks share an OTH theme, it becomes a new dimension and earlier codes are reviewed.
why_separate: Lets the data add a dimension we did not foresee.

definition: Third-party models, data, software and suppliers are vetted, traceable and covered by clear responsibilities.
includes: Procurement; supplier vetting; contracts that allocate responsibility; tracking upstream components.
borderline_decision: NIST "value chain and component integration": SUP. AWS "Governance" (best practices across the AI supply chain): SUP primary, ACC named.
why_separate: Added in v1.1 by rule 7: found under OTH in four frameworks (NIST, ISO, AWS, UK). Teams building on other companies' models depend on what they buy.

definition: The people who build, oversee or use the system understand what AI can and cannot do, and have the skills for their role.
includes: Staff AI literacy; training; competence of overseers; educating users.
borderline_decision: UK principle "You know what AI is and what its limitations are": LIT. EU AI Act Article 4: LIT.
why_separate: Added in v1.1 by rule 7: found under OTH in at least three frameworks (EU, Singapore agentic, UK; ISO possibly).
